sections.heading: Principles
sections.content: Good prompts are clear about task, format and constraints. Provide context, role, examples and evaluation criteria. Iterate and compare outputs.

sections.heading: Tactics
content: Specify role ("You are a security reviewer...")

definitions.definition: Demonstrate task with a few examples in the prompt
Constraints and checks to prevent unsafe outputs

sections.heading: What's new in 2026
sections.content: With 2026 reasoning models, prompting shifts: you often specify what “done” looks like and let the model plan, rather than micromanaging every step. Structured outputs (JSON schemas) and tool/function calling are now first-class. And a self-correcting Builder→Judge→Manager loop (see the Self-Correcting AI Loop agent) beats one long prompt for reliability on tasks that matter.
